Absolutely! Passing the NCLEX (National Council Licensure Examination) is a major milestone in becoming a registered nurse (RN) or licensed practical/vocational nurse (LPN/LVN). Here’s a comprehensive, step-by-step **NCLEX study and prep to-do list** to help you stay organized, focused, and confident.

---

🎯 **NCLEX Preparation To-Do List**

---

### ✅ 1. **Understand the Exam Basics**
- [ ] **Determine which NCLEX you're taking**:  
  - NCLEX-RN (for Registered Nurses)  
  - NCLEX-PN (for Practical/Vocational Nurses)
- [ ] **Know the exam format**:  
  - Computer Adaptive Test (CAT)  
  - 75–145 questions (RN), 85–145 questions (PN)  
  - 5 hours max (including tutorials and breaks)
- [ ] **Review the test plan**:  
  - Download the latest NCLEX test plan from [NCSBN](https://www.ncsbn.org)
  - Focus areas: Safe & Effective Care, Health Promotion, Psychosocial/Physiological Integrity

---

### ✅ 2. **Register and Schedule Your Exam**
- [ ] Apply for licensure with your state board of nursing
- [ ] Register with Pearson VUE (pay testing fee)
- [ ] Receive **ATT (Authorization to Test)** email
- [ ] Schedule your test date (Choose a date 6–8 weeks from now to allow study time)
- [ ] Confirm test location and logistics (address, ID requirements, prohibited items)

---

### ✅ 3. **Assess Your Knowledge**
- [ ] Take a **baseline practice test** (e.g., UWorld free quiz, Kaplan diagnostic)
- [ ] Identify weak areas (e.g., pharmacology, prioritization, cardiac)
- [ ] Use results to guide your study plan

---

### ✅ 4. **Create a Study Schedule (6–8 Weeks Ideal)**
- [ ] Set weekly goals and daily study blocks (1.5–3 hours/day recommended)
- [ ] Allocate time for:
  - Content review (videos, notes, textbooks)
  - Practice questions (UWorld, Kaplan, Archer, etc.)
  - Reviewing rationales
  - Full-length practice tests
- [ ] Include breaks and self-care (avoid burnout)

---

### ✅ 5. **Gather Study Resources**
- [ ] **High-Yield Review Books**:  
  - *Saunders Comprehensive Review* (favorite among students)  
  - *NCLEX Made Incredibly Easy*  
  - *UWorld QBank* (gold standard for questions)
- [ ] **Apps & Online Resources**:  
  - UWorld NCLEX app  
  - Archer NCLEX  
  - Pocket Prep  
  - Level Up RN flashcards
- [ ] **YouTube Channels**:  
  - Level Up RN  
  - Suzanne Soliman (Simple Nursing)  
  - Nurse Cheung

---

### ✅ 6. **Master Key Concepts**
- [ ] Prioritize **high-yield topics**:
  - Pharmacology (meds for cardiac, respiratory, psych, anticoagulants)
  - ABCs & Maslow’s Hierarchy
  - Safety & Infection Control (PPE, isolation precautions)
  - Delegation & Assignment (RN vs. LPN vs. UAP)
  - Lab values (Na+, K+, glucose, Hgb, creatinine)
  - Priority questions (“Which client to see first?”)
  - Acid-base balance & fluid/electrolytes

---

### ✅ 7. **Practice, Practice, Practice**
- [ ] Do **50–100 practice questions per day** (start easy, increase difficulty)
- [ ] Review **correct and incorrect answers** religiously
- [ ] Keep a **mistake journal**:
  - Record incorrect questions
  - Note why you got it wrong
  - Summarize the concept
- [ ] Take **full-length practice exams** weekly (simulate test day)

---

### ✅ 8. **Develop Test-Taking Strategies**
- [ ] Learn to **identify keywords**: e.g., “first,” “best,” “initial,” “safest”
- [ ] Use the **process of elimination**
- [ ] Answer in order of **priority** (ABCs, emergencies first)
- [ ] Use **therapeutic communication** strategies
- [ ] Practice **critical thinking**, not memorization

---

### ✅ 9. **Simulate Exam Conditions**
- [ ] Take at least **3–5 full-length exams** under timed conditions
- [ ] Replicate testing environment (quiet room, no phone)
- [ ] Practice using a whiteboard for notes (allowed at test center)

---

### ✅ 10. **Take Care of Yourself**
- [ ] Get **7–8 hours of sleep**, especially before exam day
- [ ] Eat nutritious meals
- [ ] Stay hydrated and reduce caffeine overuse
- [ ] Exercise or meditate to reduce stress
- [ ] Be kind to yourself—burnout hurts performance

---

### ✅ 11. **Final Week Prep**
- [ ] Review your **error log** and flashcards
- [ ] Light review only—no cramming
- [ ] Confirm exam date, time, location
- [ ] Know what to bring:  
  - Government-issued ID  
  - ATT (no phone, no study materials)
- [ ] Pack a snack, water, and extra layers (test center may be cold)
- [ ] Go to bed early the night before

---

### ✅ 12. **Exam Day Success**
- [ ] Arrive **30 minutes early**
- [ ] Use the tutorial time to relax and warm up
- [ ] Breathe; flag hard questions and move on
- [ ] Stay calm—CAT adapts, so difficulty means you're on the right track!
- [ ] Use all 5 hours if needed; don’t rush

---

### ✅ 13. **After the Exam**
- [ ] Celebrate — you did it!
- [ ] Sign up for **Quick Results** (NCSBN) if available (3 business days, ~$7.95)
- [ ] Official results arrive in 2–4 weeks via your board
- [ ] If not passed: retake in 45 days—learn from results and retest

---

🎉 **Final Encouragement**:  
The NCLEX is challenging but **100% passable** with focused prep and resilience. You’ve already made it through nursing school—this is the final step!

Stay consistent. Breathe. You’ve got this.

💬 Need help adjusting this list to your timeline or learning style? I'm here to help!
